decisive_items: He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily.
On day 9 of therapy, he reported loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice

Laboratory studies showed leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL, AST 175 U/L (0–40), ALT 402 U/L (0–55), alkaline phosphatase 235 U/L (15–250), γ-glutamyl transferase 327 U/L (8–61), total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2), and direct bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL (0–0.25)
response.rationale: R2 uniquely integrates the Alfuzosin start, the day-9 symptom onset, and the hepatocellular-predominant laboratory injury after negative viral/autoimmune/metabolic/biliary workup. R4 captures only the elevated transaminases and ignores jaundice/bilirubin/biliary exclusion, while R3 is less consistent because ALP is normal and ALT is disproportionately elevated, so neither offers a complete etiologic diagnosis.

rejected.why: Describes a cholestatic pattern rather than an etiologic diagnosis; ALP is normal and ALT is much higher, so cholestasis is not the best characterization.
